title: Rentosertib (ISM001-055): First Fully AI-Discovered Target and Generative AI Drug Shows Phase 2a Clinical Efficacy
whyItMatters: Published in Nature Medicine, Insilico Medicine’s rentosertib became the first drug with both an AI-discovered biological target (TNIK) and AI-generated molecule to report positive randomized Phase 2a human clinical efficacy.
summary: Published in Nature Medicine on June 3, 2025, a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a clinical trial (GENESIS-IPF, 71 patients across 22 sites) evaluated rentosertib (ISM001-055), an investigational small-molecule inhibitor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Both the novel fibrotic disease target (TNIK kinase) and the drug’s chemical structure were generated by Insilico Medicine’s Pharma.AI platform (PandaOmics target discovery + Chemistry42 generative design) in roughly 18 months from target hypothesis to preclinical candidate. Over 12 weeks, patients receiving 60 mg once daily achieved a mean forced vital capacity (FVC) increase of +98.4 mL compared with −20.3 mL on placebo, with comparable safety across arms.
technicalHighlights: First peer-reviewed Phase 2a randomized human trial where both the novel biological target (TNIK) and small-molecule inhibitor were generated by AI.
60 mg once-daily arm achieved +98.4 mL mean FVC lung-function improvement (95% CI 10.9–185.9) vs. −20.3 mL placebo over 12 weeks.
Compressed target-to-preclinical-candidate discovery from typical 4–5 years down to ~18 months, advancing toward Phase 3 trials.
caveats: Phase 2a trial was relatively small (71 patients) and short (12 weeks, conducted in China); larger, longer global Phase 2b/3 trials are required to confirm durable clinical benefit and long-term safety.

scoreRationale.foundational: Crucial clinical proof-of-concept that end-to-end generative AI target identification and molecular design can translate into measurable efficacy in human patients.
scoreRationale.ripple: Sets a clinical benchmark for the entire AI-driven pharmaceutical industry after years of preclinical-only milestones and early Phase 1 discontinuations.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a human clinical trial published in Nature Medicine.
scoreRationale.velocity: Cut target-to-preclinical discovery timeline roughly in half before entering human clinical testing.
